title: VerifyPermitRequest
description: Wire payload sent to POST /v1-verify-permit. Read by atlasent-api/supabase/functions/v1-verify-permit/handler.ts. Only `permit_token` is required server-side; `action_type` and `actor_id` are cross-checked when present and yield ACTION_TYPE_MISMATCH / ACTOR_MISMATCH on disagreement. The legacy {decision_id, action, agent, api_key} shape is no longer canonical — SDKs may accept legacy fields as input with a deprecation warning, but MUST always serialize to the wire shape described here.

permit_token.description: The permit_token returned by a prior /v1-evaluate call.

action_type.description: Optional cross-check — re-state the action_type. ACTION_TYPE_MISMATCH if it disagrees with the original evaluation.

actor_id.description: Optional cross-check — re-state the actor_id. ACTOR_MISMATCH if it disagrees with the original evaluation.

require_approval.description: Caller assertion that this consume must produce a permit row with a populated approval binding. When true and the row carries no binding, the verifier returns APPROVAL_LINKAGE_MISSING (valid=false, consumed=true). Use this when calling on behalf of an action whose human-approval requirement isn't covered by the action_type-prefix heuristic on the server.

operation_intent_id.description: 2026-08-13: optional cross-check — re-present the operation_intent_id supplied at evaluate time (see evaluate-request.schema.json). When the permit carries a bound operation_intent_id and the presented value disagrees (or is omitted where the binding requires it), the verifier denies PERMIT_BINDING_MISMATCH — the same frozen verify_error_code already used for a target_id disagreement, not a new code.

actor_identity.description: 2026-10-10 (atlasent-api#3915): optional actor_identity.v1 assertion for the PERMIT's actor, forwarded unchanged. Required when the action class's server-owned execution_principal_binding is `verified_actor` (ACTOR_IDENTITY_REQUIRED when omitted, ACTOR_IDENTITY_INVALID when it does not verify against the permit's actor, action type, tenant and environment). Ignored in every other mode, so presenting one is always safe. The caller cannot choose or downgrade the mode.
